Prescribing Information Links
How much should I expect to pay for Zepbound® (tirzepatide)?

The list price1 of Zepbound is $499 - $1,086.37 per fill, but the amount you pay will largely depend on your prescription drug insurance plan.

If you have commercial drug insurance with coverage for Zepbound, you may be eligible to pay as low as $25 for a one- or three-month supply Zepbound single-dose pens. Governmental beneficiaries excluded. Eligibility required, terms and conditions apply. Savings subject to monthly and annual limits. Month is defined as 28-days and up to 4 single-dose pens. Card eligibility and terms and conditions may be terminated, rescinded, revoked, or amended by Lilly at any time without notice and for any reason. PROGRAM IS NOT INSURANCE. Review full terms and conditions at https://zepbound.lilly.com/coverage-savings#terms-and-conditions.

Regardless of insurance status, there are resources available to help you.

Available through Zepbound self-pay, Zepbound is offered as a 4-count single-dose vial (0.5mL) and a single-patient-use KwikPen (2.4mL, 0.6mL/dose) in doses of 2.5mg, 5mg, 7.5mg, 10mg, 12.5mg and 15mg, with direct-to-patient pricing of $299, $399, $499, $699, $699 and $699 respectively.2

To learn more about Zepbound self-pay options, please visit: https://zepbound.lilly.com/coverage-savings.
To find out if you qualify for Medicaid and for information about copayments in your state, please visit: https://www.medicaid.gov/resources-for-states.
To learn more about private individual policies via the Insurance Marketplace, please visit: https://americasmedicines.com/education/health-insurance-resources.

For the most accurate information, talk to your insurance provider who knows the details of your plan.

See Indication and Safety Summary, including Warnings.

Go to zepbound.lilly.com
Want More Information?

Go to zepbound.lilly.com for additional savings and support resources and information. If you have additional questions, you can click on the chatbot icon on any page of the Zepbound website. Although we won't replace the advice of your healthcare provider, we'll do our best to help you.

1 List price, also referred to as wholesale acquisition cost or WAC, is the price at which Lilly sells its products to wholesalers. The prices patients pay at the pharmacy may be different and largely depend on the out-of-pocket costs set by their insurance provider, pharmacy charges, and/or discounts or financial assistance that may be available to the patient. WAC from AnalySource accessed on January 1, 2026. Reprinted with permission by First Databank, Inc. All rights reserved. ©2026. https://www.fdbhealth.com/policies/drug-pricing-policy. A monthly supply of Zepbound is defined as 28 days per month.

2 Lilly USA LLC's direct to patient price is the price at which Lilly sells the product directly to patients. The direct to patient price is not the WAC, as the product is only available for purchase by cash paying patients.
